QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_43

question.text: What is the role of co-location/proximity hosting services offered by exchanges?

answer.text: Co-location/proximity hosting lets stock brokers and data vendors place their systems within or close to the exchange premises and connect to the exchange trading platform through a direct private network for low-latency access
Co-location gives certain members faster access to market data than others, creating a legitimate speed advantage
Co-location is available only to clearing members and is prohibited for trading-only members
Co-location services are provided free of cost by exchanges as part of their obligation to ensure fair access

explanation.text: The Logic: Co-location/proximity hosting allows stock brokers and data vendors to locate their systems within or close to the exchange premises and connect to the exchange trading platform through a direct private network. This shortens the network path and supports low-latency access to the trading platform. The Trap: Co-location is not free, is not restricted to clearing members, and is not a mechanism for granting unequal speed advantages between participants. Note: The source describes co-location in terms of proximity and direct private-network connectivity. Any further fair-access/same-latency policy claims should be backed by an explicit regulatory source.
